title: Canonical cycle evaluation and homology descent for a zero-differential source
statement: For a small ringed site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], integer-indexed complexes E,K [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with zero differential on E and any integer n, let P=Hom(E,K) [def-pur-hom-complex] with the fixed projections [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections]. There exist f:H^n(P)->Hom(H^(-n)(E),H^0(K)) [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and c:Z^n(P)->Hom(Z^(-n)(E),Z^0(K)), satisfying the two evaluation factorization identities displayed verbatim in lean.statement. Neither map is claimed invertible; no boundedness, freeness, or concentration is assumed.

proof.text: Use the Hom differential formula to show that evaluation on cycles lands in K cycles. Lift through K.iCycles via the proved upstream tensorHomEquiv, which converts the lift to the kernel universal property. Internal Hom preserves monos by tensorHomAdjunction.

The Hom differential formula in degrees n-1,n expresses evaluation of a Hom boundary on an E cycle as a K boundary. Cancel the internal Hom of K.iCycles (a mono), then apply K.toCycles_comp_homologyπ. Descend through P.homologyIsCokernel.

Zero E differential makes E.homologyπ(-n) invertible by HomologicalComplex.isIso_homologyπ. Precompose the descended map with its inverse. Composition of homObjMap and the inverse identity give the second factorization; the kernel lift gives the first.

theorem finiteFreeZero_homologyEvaluation_cycles
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {S : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf S CommRingCat.{u})
    (E K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose S (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ)
    (n : ℤ)
    (hzero : ∀ a b : ℤ, E.d a b = 0) :
    let P := homComplex (R := R) E K
    let π := (Classical.choose (homComplex_projections_exists (R := R)))
      E K n (-n) 0 (by omega)
    ∃ f : P.homology n ⟶ SheafOfModules.homObj (R := R)
        (E.homology (-n)) (K.homology 0),
      ∃ c : P.cycles n ⟶
        SheafOfModules.homObj (R := R) (E.cycles (-n)) (K.cycles 0),
      c ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) (𝟙 _) (K.iCycles 0) =
        P.iCycles n ≫ π ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) (E.iCycles (-n)) (𝟙 _) ∧
      c ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) (𝟙 _) (K.homologyπ 0) =
        P.homologyπ n ≫ f ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) (E.homologyπ (-n)) (𝟙 _)
